report.source_text: Histology demonstrated features of classic HL involving spinal cord parenchyma and peripheral nerve fascicles. The tumor tissue was composed of scattered Hodgkin cells, Reed–Sternberg cells and lacunar cells surrounded by a mix of small lymphocytes, histiocytes, eosinophils and occasional neutrophils (Figure 2). No prominent fibrous bands were present and, therefore, the mixed cellularity subtype was favored. On immunohistochemistry, the tumor cells showed membrane staining for CD30.

clinician.final_diagnosis: classic HL involving spinal cord parenchyma and peripheral nerve fascicles
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 48-year-old female presented with a 2-month history of lower back pain and progressive neurological symptoms including right L5-S1 radiculopathy, perianal paresthesia, and anal/urinary sphincter dysfunction. Spinal MRI revealed a lobulated, enhancing exophytic lesion involving the conus medullaris and filum terminale at L1/2, with cord edema, and a smaller lesion in the cauda equina at L5/S1. A biopsy of these lesions confirmed classic Hodgkin Lymphoma (mixed cellularity subtype) involving spinal cord parenchyma and peripheral nerve fascicles, characterized by Hodgkin and Reed-Sternberg cells, and CD30 positivity. Whole-body PET/CT ruled out further CNS involvement or systemic disease. The patient received radiotherapy, leading to complete resolution of symptoms (no motor deficit, normal bowel/bladder function) and MRI findings (resolution of enhancement at L1/2 and L5/S1) at 10 months postoperatively.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with progressive lower back pain, radiculopathy, perianal paresthesia, and anal/urinary sphincter dysfunction.
Spinal MRI revealed a lobulated, homogenously enhancing exophytic lesion (13x14x22 mm) involving the conus medullaris and filum terminale at L1/2, with cord edema extending to T11.
A small 5mm enhancing lesion was also noted in the cauda equina at L5/S1 on MRI.
Histology from the spinal lesion biopsy demonstrated features of classic Hodgkin Lymphoma, specifically involving spinal cord parenchyma and peripheral nerve fascicles.
The tumor tissue was composed of scattered Hodgkin cells, Reed–Sternberg cells, and lacunar cells, with a mixed cellularity subtype favored.
Immunohistochemistry showed tumor cells with membrane staining for CD30.
Whole body PET/CT was negative for further CNS involvement or systemic disease.
At 10 months postoperatively, the patient was well with no motor deficit and normal bowel and bladder function.
Follow-up MRI showed complete resolution of enhancement at the L1/2 level and the nodule at L5/S1 post-radiotherapy.
